newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Hindustan Times
TAMIL MAANILA CONGRESS RULES OUT MERGER

Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) leader G.K. Moopanar firmly ruled out a merger with the Congress. The TMC was floated in deference to the wishes of the cadres in Tamil Nadu and the general mood among the partymen was not in favour of a merger with the Congress, he said. Moopanar said no significance should be attached to his recent meeting with Congress president Sitaram Kesri.
The Times Of India
CHAIRMAN, FOUR DIRECTORS OF ITC TO BE SACKED

Five full-time directors of ITC Ltd, including its chairman Y.C. Deveshwar, are likely to be sacked shortly. Sources said a decision to this effect had been taken at the top level in the government. An entirely new team would replace these directors, but the new incumbents would not be nominees of BAT Industries, the single major share-holder of ITC, sources indicated. The new chairman would also be an executive chairman. Sources said the decision had been taken because it was felt by the prime minister's office that a large company like ITC could not be allowed to function with most of its directors under the Enforcement Directorate's scrutiny.
The Economic Times

HARVARD, STANFORD AND TORONTO POOL TO INVEST IN INDIA The $7-billion President & Fellows of Harvard College, the University of Toronto Global Pool and the Stanford University Endowment funds are keen to directly invest in the Indian market and register with the bourse regulator (SEBI). Harvard College and Toronto Pool have already applied, while Stanford University has approached SEBI through its fund managers. Sources said several funds had approached the SEBI following the finance minister's announcement saying that investment through the FII-route would be opened up further to include university funds endowments, foundations or charitable trusts or societies. According to sources, the government may allow also proprietorial funds to invest in Indian markets.
ENVIRONMENT ACT TO BE AMENDED

The government plans to grant more autonomy to states, under the Environment Protection Act, to clear power projects seeking their approval. It is working out the modalities for delegation of power under the new Act. The move was follows demands by various state governments for more functional autonomy, the environment and forest secretary said. Prior to the granting of autonomy, the state pollution control boards would be asked to upgrade their capacity to be able to handle matters, he said. The grant of autonomy would help speed up the clearance of power projects in the states, he added.
FEEDSTOCK AVAILABILITY TO DECIDE POWER TARIFFS

The National Task Force (NTF) on power has decided to base the principles for fixing tariff of thermal stations on the availability of feedstock material rather than on plant load factor. Hitherto, power plants used to measure tariff on the basis of the plant load factor at which the plants operated. The NTF has also decided to introduce merit order operation of power plants calling for obtaining maximum power with minimum cost. Sources said the Central Electricity Authority was likely to evolve a proper mechanism in the near future for introducing merit order operation.
Financial Express
SERVICE TAX ON ADVERTISING COMES INTO EFFECT

Five percent service tax on advertising (Ads) has been made effective from November 1. As per the notice issued by the Commissioner of Central excise, the tax has been levied on the agency commission of 15 percent. However, the amount paid by the agency for displaying Ads in the print and electronic media have been exempted from the tax bracket. According to industry observers this move may affect the profitability of the Ad-industry which is already bogged down by the liquidity crunch and the one percent TDS charged on gross amount. The growth of the Ad-industry is pegged at 15 percent for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) as compared to 35.6 percent in 1995/96.
TWO-WHEELER MAKERS, GOVERNMENT DISAGREE ON NEW NORMS

The two-wheeler manufacturers did not seem to be in agreement with the government over emission norms to be implemented by the year 2000. The new emission standards proposed by the government aim to halve the exhaust emission from the 1996 level. Almost the entire two-wheeler industry would find it difficult to meet the new standards due to lack of proper technology. The norms, to be notified shortly, would affect almost all two-wheeler manufacturers including Bajaj Auto, LML, Hero Honda, Hero Motors, Escorts and TVS-Suzuki.
Business Standard
TATA GROUP SALES UP 22.7 PCT

Combined sales of the 84 Tata group companies grew by 22.7 percent during fiscal 1995/96 (April-March). The group sales were put at 295 billion rupees, up from 240 billion rupees in 1994/95. Estimated total income went up by 22.3 percent to 302 billion rupees from 247 billion in the previous fiscal. Profit before tax went up 25 percent from 21.2 billion rupees to 26.5 billion rupees. Total value of assets of the group companies increased from 235.17 billion rupees to 270 billion rupees.
The Observer
INDIA TO STRIVE FOR A 1.5 PCT SHARE IN WORLD AGRO TRADE

Agro exports from India have reached a level of $2.43 billion as against $575 million five years ago. Agro-exports formed about 18 percent of India's total exports last year. India's share in the world agro market is one percent. Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaia said India should try to increase its share in the world agro market to 1.5 percent by 2000 AD and five percent by 2010 AD.
GEM, JEWELLERY EXPORTS DECLINE TO $2,457 MLN

Gems and Jewellery exports showed a decline in the provisional export figures for the first half of the current fiscal (April-March). The export figures stood at $2,457 million as against $2,524 million recorded during the last corresponding period. Given the current outlook, the export target of $6300 million set for 1996/97 for this sector may be difficult to achieve. The down trend in exports was mainly attributed to the central bank (RBI)'s decision to hike the post-shipment credit and the routing of import documents through banks.
Business Line
INDIA SLATED TO PRODUCE 37 MT STEEL BY 2000 AD

Steel and Mines Minister B.P. Baishya has called for setting up more steel plants to boost the economy. The current capacity is about 22 million tonnes per annum. The government was taking many corrective measure to increase production, the minister informed. These included liberalisation, removal of control over pricing and distribution and giving the buyer option to trade in the international market. 20 new proposals (200 billion rupees) for steel plants had been cleared and eight more (90 billion rupees) were about to be cleared. With these, India was slated to produce 37 million tonnes of steel by year 2000, the minister said.
